keyword: how long does it take to get to the moon from earth
claims: Crewed spacecraft typically take about 3 days to travel from Earth to the Moon.
The Apollo 8 mission set a record of 69 hours and 8 minutes for travel from Earth to the Moon.
Spacecraft travel time from Earth to the Moon can vary from just over 8 hours for high-speed flybys to over a month for fuel-efficient robotic missions.
Apollo missions typically took around 3-4 days to enter lunar orbit.
Apollo 11 took 4 days, 6 hours, and 45 minutes to enter lunar orbit.
Artemis II is the 2026 crewed mission.
Artemis II is expected to take around 5-6 days to reach the Moon.
ESA's Smart-1 took 13 months to travel to the Moon.
The Moon is about 238,855 miles (384,400 km) from Earth.
Spacecraft travel to the Moon at speeds of 24,500 mph.
Trips from Earth to the Moon are slowed by Earth's gravity.
